newsitem.title: ITALY: Court orders retrial in "Monster of Florence" case.
newsitem.headline: Court orders retrial in "Monster of Florence" case.

text.p: Italy's highest court ordered the retrial on Thursday of an elderly farmer cleared of the "Monster of Florence" serial sex murders.
Reopening one of the grisliest criminal cases in post-war Italy, the Court of Cassation overturned the acquittal of Pietro Pacciani last February by the Florence court of appeal.
A lower court had found Pacciani, now in his 70s, guilty of seven double murders in November 1994.
The killer, dubbed the "Monster of Florence" by the Italian media, shot the victims in isolated countryside near the Tuscan capital and mutilated the women's bodies.
Four of the 14 dead, all killed between 1968 and 1985, were foreign tourists and all but two were courting couples.
It was not immediately clear when Pacciani's new trial would take place. The Court of Cassation ruled that it should be heard by a different panel of judges from the Florence appeal court.
Pacciani, a farm labourer, had argued at his trials that he was "as innocent as Christ on the Cross". He has been free from custody since February and did not attend Thursday's hearing.
The Court of Cassation heard an appeal from the prosecution, which had argued that the Florence court failed to admit late evidence from four alleged new witnesses to one of the killings.
"I hope this new trial will take place as soon as possible because we are tired of suffering," said Renzo Rontini, whose daughter Pia was killed in 1984 with her boyfriend Claudio Stefanacci.
Pacciani's lawyer Nino Marazzita said he had no worries about the case being re-opened.
"I am sure that I can show once again...that Pacciani is innocent," Marazzita told reporters.
